quick.summary: How to map your stakeholders so everyone gets exactly what they need.
quick.takeaway: Group people by their power and interest to manage their updates.

parts.title: Who needs to know

beats.line: I copied the whole floor on my report and the director got mad. Why?
Think of a busy kitchen. Does the dishwasher need to know the soup recipe?
No, they just need to know which pots to scrub.
Right. Not everyone at work needs the exact same level of detail.
Treating everyone equally actually creates noise, which blocks the real decisions.
We plot people on a stakeholder matrix.
Can I just call it sorting my crowd?
Perfect. You sort your crowd based on two simple things.
So how do I know who goes where?

parts.cliff: Next time: Finding out who actually holds the keys.

beats.line: To sort your crowd, you ask two questions.
First, how much power do they have? Second, do they care?
The director has power, but she does not care about my pipeline script.
Right. High power, low interest. Keep her happy, but do not flood her.

board.text: High power, low care = keep happy

beats.line: What about the analysts? They care a lot, but cannot approve the budget.
Low power, high interest. Keep them informed. They are your cheerleaders.

board.text: Low power, high care = keep informed

beats.line: And my manager has high power and cares a lot.
Yes. Manage them closely. They need all the details.
I send a summary to the director and the script to the analysts.
Your inbox will be a much happier place.

quiz.question: A user of your dashboard cares deeply about changes but has no authority. How do you handle them?
options: Manage them closely with daily meetings.
Keep them satisfied with high level summaries.
quiz.explanation: People with high interest but low power need to be kept informed so they stay supportive.

quiz.question: Everyone in the company should receive the exact same level of detail about your project.
quiz.explanation: Giving everyone the same details creates noise. You must tailor the message to their power and interest.
